import unittest

from ring import RingBuffer


class TestRingBuffer(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_write_read_basic(self):
        rb = RingBuffer(3)
        rb.write(1)
        rb.write(2)
        rb.write(3)
        self.assertEqual(rb.read(), [1])
        self.assertEqual(rb.read(2), [2, 3])

    def test_overwrite_when_full(self):
        rb = RingBuffer(3)
        for i in range(5):
            rb.write(i)
        # After writing 0..4 into capacity 3, oldest (0,1) overwritten.
        self.assertEqual(rb.read(3), [2, 3, 4])

    def test_read_does_not_past_write_pointer(self):
        rb = RingBuffer(3)
        rb.write('a')
        rb.write('b')
        # Only 2 items available; read more than available returns just those.
        self.assertEqual(rb.read(10), ['a', 'b'])
        # Nothing left.
        self.assertEqual(rb.read(), [])

    def test_overwrite_then_read_advances_head(self):
        rb = RingBuffer(2)
        for i in range(4):  # writes 0,1,2,3 -> keeps [2,3]
            rb.write(i)
        self.assertEqual(rb.read(), [2])
        self.assertEqual(rb.read(), [3])
        # Buffer empty; writing again works.
        rb.write('x')
        self.assertEqual(rb.read(), ['x'])


if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()
